nodes.name: Microwave-assisted PtRu alloying on WO₃
nodes.procedure: NaH₂PO₂·H₂O, Pt(acac)₂, Ru(acac)₃, and WO₃ hydrate (after hydrothermal treatment to form 2D WO₃-Oᵥ support) are thoroughly mixed. The mixture is transferred to a quartz boat, and then 30 μL of deionized water is added and stirred to form a homogeneous paste (Figure S1a). Microwave-assisted reaction for 60 s yields a dark blue powder (Figure S1b). The product is then washed at 80°C to produce the final PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ sample.

nodes.description: HER LSV performance in 1 M KOH (three-electrode)
nodes.source_text: The hydrogen evolution performance of prepared samples in 1 M KOH is evaluated using the three-electrode system. Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) polarization curves are shown in Figure 3a. PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ exhibits an ultra-low overpotential of 9 mV at 10 mA cm⁻². The Tafel slope is 25.4 mV dec⁻¹ for PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ. At overpotentials of 50, 100, and 150 mV, the TOF values for PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ are 1.33, 2.74, and 4.02 s⁻¹.

nodes.description: HER LSV performance in 1 M KOH + seawater (three-electrode)
nodes.source_text: Figure 4a displays the LSV curves of the prepared samples. In the 1 M KOH + seawater electrolyte, PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ demonstrates robust HER activity with an overpotential of 26 mV at 10 mA cm⁻². The Tafel plot (Figure 4b) shows that PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ has the lowest Tafel slope (26.4 mV dec⁻¹).

nodes.description: HER LSV performance in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ (three-electrode)
nodes.source_text: PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ still exhibits optimal hydrogen evolution performance (Figure 5a-c), with an extremely low overpotential of 6 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² and Tafel slope of 20.2 mV dec⁻¹. At an overpotential of 19 mV (equivalent to PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ at 50 mA cm⁻²), the mass activity and TOF values for PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ are 5.7 and 5.3 times that of commercial Pt/C, respectively.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in two-electrode system
nodes.source_text: The PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ@NiFe // NiFe system operating OWS achieves lower potential than the Pt/C@NiFe // RuO₂@NiFe system. The PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ@NiFe // NiFe system demonstrates good reversibility and negligible decay in multi-step chronoamperometry and 10-h I-t tests. The actual gas production ratio at the cathode and anode is 1.91:1, close to the theoretical ratio of 2:1.

nodes.description: HER double-layer capacitance measurement in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: As shown in Figure 3d, the C_dl values of Pt/WO₃-Oᵥ, Ru/WO₃-Oᵥ, and WO₃-Oᵥ are at a lower level. Following Ru incorporation, the C_dl value of PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ increased nearly 3.7 times.

nodes.description: HER stability tests in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: After 2500 cyclic voltammetry (CV) and 10-h chronoamperometric test, PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ exhibited negligible degradation, demonstrating good stability (Figure 3f and inset).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanoclusters uniformly distributed on the support with average particle size of ≈5.87 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) characterization further analyzes the structure of PtRu / WO₃·Oᵥ. Figure 1d illustrates the distribution of nanoclusters on the support, showing an average particle size of ≈5.87 nm with a uniform distribution.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes of ≈0.372 nm corresponding to WO₃ (110) plane and ≈0.223 nm aligning with Pt (111) plane (0.226 nm), indicating lattice contraction from Ru integration suggesting PtRu alloy formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images provide clear crystal plane information for PtRu / WO₃·Oᵥ. Figure 1e shows lattice fringes with a spacing of ≈0.372 nm, corresponding to the (110) plane of WO₃. Figure 1f shows nanoclusters with lattice fringes ≈0.223 nm aligning with the (111) plane of Pt (0.226 nm), indicating lattice contraction from Ru integration into Pt and suggesting the formation of PtRu alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping reveals uniform distribution of W, O, Pt, and Ru elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDX) elemental mapping images (Figure 1g) reveal the uniform distribution of W, O, Pt, and Ru elements in PtRu / WO₃·Oᵥ.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern corresponds to tetragonal WO₃ phase and cubic Pt phase with high-angle shift indicating lattice contraction from PtRu alloy integration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of PtRu / WO₃ - Oᵥ corresponds closely to the tetragonal WO₃ phase (PDF#04-006-7232) and the cubic Pt phase (PDF#04-003-6500).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show characteristic peaks at 242.11, 318.29, 679.88, and 801.37 cm⁻¹ for W-O-W vibrations with intensity change at 679.88 cm⁻¹ reflecting Oᵥ impact.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b displays Raman spectra of the prepared samples. Characteristic peaks near 242.11 and 318.29 cm⁻¹ indicate W-O-W bending vibrations and peaks at 679.88 and 801.37 cm⁻¹ suggest W-O-W stretching vibrations.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows strongest signal at g=2.003 for PtRu/WO₃-Oᵥ attributed to unpaired electrons trapped by increased Oᵥ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) results show a distinct signal at g = 2.003 (Figure 2c), attributed to unpaired electrons trapped by Oᵥ in WO₃. After undergoing microwave reactions and PtRu integration, PtRu / WO₃ - Oᵥ shows the strongest signal for increased Oᵥ.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS W 4f shows peaks at 36.10 eV (4f7/2) and 38.20 eV (4f5/2) for W6+ with positive shift vs WO3-Ov indicating electron loss; Pt 4f shows Pt0 at 71.25/74.60 eV and Pt2+ at 72.40/75.70 eV with negative shift indicating electron gain; O 1s shows lattice oxygen at 530.30 eV and Ov at 532.40 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2d shows the high-resolution W 4f spectrum. Due to spin-orbit splitting, deconvolution revealed peaks at 4f7/2 and 4f5/2, characteristic of W6+... the 4f7/2 and 4f5/2 orbitals of PtRu / WO3 - Ov (36.10 eV; 38.20 eV)... The high-resolution Pt 4f spectrum shown in Figure 2e exhibits two main peaks at Pt 4f7/2 and Pt 4f5/2. For Pt / WO3 - Ov, the binding energy near 71.25 and 74.60 eV correspond to Pt0 species... PtRu / WO3 - Ov exhibits a negative shift... PtRu / WO3 - Ov exhibits a slight positive shift in O 1s orbital... Peaks at 530.30 and 530.18 eV are from the lattice oxygen... Peaks at 532.40 and 532.38 eV indicate Ov.
